hints.title: Perfect Binary Tree Criteria
hints.text: A tree is perfect if and only if both left and right subtrees are perfect and have identical heights.

hints.title: Post-Order Height Return
hints.text: Return the height h of the perfect subtree rooted at the current node, or -1 if the subtree is not perfect. Size is 2^h - 1.

hints.title: Collection and K-th Selection
hints.text: Collect all valid perfect subtree sizes, sort in descending order, and return the k-th largest element (or -1 if fewer than k exist).

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
# Definition for a binary tree node.
class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right

class Solution:
    def kthLargestPerfectSubtree(self, root: 'TreeNode', k: int) -> int:
        perfect_sizes = []
        
        # Returns height of perfect subtree rooted at node, or -1 if not perfect
        def dfs(node):
            if not node:
                return 0
            lh = dfs(node.left)
            rh = dfs(node.right)
            if lh != -1 and rh != -1 and lh == rh:
                h = lh + 1
                perfect_sizes.append((1 << h) - 1)
                return h
            return -1
            
        dfs(root)
        perfect_sizes.sort(reverse=True)
        if len(perfect_sizes) < k:
            return -1
        return perfect_sizes[k - 1]
```

variables: n: number of nodes in binary tree
complexity.notes: Post-order traversal visits all n nodes in O(n). Sorting collected sizes takes O(n log n).
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Checking perfection independently for every node takes O(n^2) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(n) recursion stack and collection list.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Combines bottom-up post-order DFS subtree validation with descending size selection.
